# Lumber Hall: a timber wholesaler's market hall, through the block

Identity: a twin-gabled half-timbered burgage warehouse (Hanseatic Speicher type) running from the north street to
the south street. Each street sees the same face: two great slate gables, each with stacked loading doors and a
hoist beam at the apex, jettied twice over a ground-floor row of three wood merchants (a Folio plus its door
stalls each). One wood per business, shown in its own logs, planks and leaves. Stair lobby at the west end and a
cart passage through the block at the east end.

## Build library (`tools/src/build.mjs`)

```js
import { load, Grid, guard, tile, mirrorX, mirrorZ, shell, carve, replace, B, face, DIRS } from ".../tools/src/build.mjs";
const g = guard(load("in.nbt"));          // or: new Grid([w, h, d], { dataVersion })
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "south", "top"));   // [block, state] helpers: stairs slab log wood trapdoor door fence wall lantern chain wallTorch pane block
g.fill([x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1], "stone_bricks");
tile(g, { from: 1, step: 4, to: 19 }, (z, i) => bay(z, i));  // the bay rhythm
mirrorX(g, cx, (set) => set(x, y, z, block, state));          // symmetric pair, facings mirrored
shell(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", { floor: true, ceiling: false });
carve(g, a, b);                            // stores air (clears the cell on placement)
replace(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", "stone_bricks");
g.save("out.nbt");                          // never overwrite the input
console.log(g.refused);                     // guarded writes that were refused (report them)
```

Shape brushes (also exported from `build.mjs`): curved forms — `dome`, `cylinder`, `minaret`, `arch` (+ `circleCells`,
`ring`, `disc`, `revolve`) — see `shapes-curved.md`; massing — `setbacks`, `gableRoof`, `hipRoof`, `fins`, `parapet`,
`cornice`, `falseFront`, `stepGable` — see `shapes-massing.md`. Each is `fn(g, opts)`, writes through `g.set` (so
`guard()` still protects function), and returns `{cells, refused, bounds}`.

`guard(grid)` refuses writes into the grid's functional cells and their keep-clear cells (or a set you pass);
it never throws — check `g.refused`. `runParts(g, [["shell", shell.build], ["garden", garden.build]], { palette:
"palette.json" })` runs a build's parts in order so each can only add into air: writes into an earlier part's cells
(air included) are refused and reported, the ground laid before it stays writable, and blocks outside the palette
are reported per part. With `roof: "roof.json"` (a `mcd roof --spec` file) it lays the roof right after the first
part, so later parts build around it instead of the roof tool clearing attics and gables after them; no file yet means
the roof is skipped with a note. A part given `{ carve: true }` as a third element (the stair joiner) may cut through
earlier floors and ceilings (cells with air straight above or below), never walls. `mcd reskin in.nbt out.nbt --swap
spruce=dark_oak,red=blue[,bricks=mud_bricks] [--box ...]` swaps materials on a finished build, form for form, states
kept (a wood or dye word swaps every block named with it; a full block id swaps itself and its stairs, slab and wall);
`mcd variant <run> --name n [--swap ...] [--roof '{json}']` does it into `<run>/variants/n/` with a card, re-running
the build's code when the roof changes. `mcd overworld palette.json [--write]` lists (drops) nether and end blocks. The Grid keeps block-entity NBT (sign text, chest contents) and entities and
writes them back unchanged; cells you don't touch round-trip byte-for-byte.

Grow the box with `g.resize([w, h, d], [dx, dy, dz])` (a shift grows toward −); a shift moves every coordinate,
so re-derive any contract coordinates after shifting.

## Banners, signs and other block entities

Banners, signs, chests, beds, bells, mob heads, decorated pots and shulker boxes are entity-rendered in vanilla, and
`mcd render` draws them with their entity models and textures:
- **Banners:** the cloth in its base colour plus every dyed pattern from the block entity.
- **Signs:** their text, glowing text drawn brighter.
- **Other entity-rendered blocks:** a neutral box, listed under `unknownBlocks` as "entity-rendered, approximated".

Author banners and signs with the build helpers. Each returns `[block, state, nbt]` with valid block-entity NBT
that round-trips through save and load:

```js
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("cyan", [["stripe_center", "white"], ["border", "black"]], { facing: "north" }));   // wall banner
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("red", [["cross", "yellow"]], { wall: false, rotation: 8 }));                       // standing, faces north
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.sign("spruce", ["PERMIT", "OFFICE"], { facing: "north", color: "black", glow: false }));
```
- **Banner patterns:** `stripe_center`, `stripe_top`, `stripe_bottom`, `stripe_left`, `stripe_right`,
  `stripe_middle`, `border`, `curly_border`, `cross`, `straight_cross`, `rhombus`, `circle`, `flower`, `globe`,
  `gradient`, `gradient_up`, `half_horizontal`, `half_vertical`, `triangle_top`, `triangle_bottom`, `bricks`,
  `small_stripes`, `diagonal_left`, `diagonal_right` (the full list is under `textures/entity/banner/`).
- **Colours:** the 16 dye names.
- **NBT format:** banners use the 1.20.5+ `patterns` list (`legacy: true` writes the older `Patterns` /
  `Pattern` / `Color` form). Sign text is written as JSON components below data version 4325 (1.21.5) and as plain
  string components from 1.21.5 on (`dataVersion` option; the grid's default is 1.21.4).
- **Standing `rotation`:** 0 faces south, 4 west, 8 north, 12 east. Wall banners and signs hang on the block behind
  them and face `facing`.

## Review card

One image of a build for a glance or a reviewer (prints one JSON object; non-zero exit and a stderr message on error):

- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out card.png [--tiles dir] [--front n] [--reuse]` — render (close-ups, `MCD_TILE_SCALE=2`) and compose the card (street | front-left, front-right | back, plus the roof close-up row; tiles fit 700x700, white). `--reuse` skips the render when `dir/street.png` exists. `{"card","tiles","views":[...]}`
- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out eye.png --tiles dir --layout eye` — the eye-level card: only what a player sees from the ground (street | down-the-street left, right | back), sky trimmed, so a roof weighs what it weighs in the game.

## Inspection

Cheap, deterministic checks to run after every pass, before judging a render by eye. Each has `--json`.

- **Glance and close-ups** — `$MCD render house.nbt --closeups --tiles tiles/` adds a row of tiles to the sheet: a
  *glance* tile (the street view at 320 px: what reads at a glance) and close-ups at ≥ 12 px per block of the
  entrance (door cells), the eave band, each facade's busiest region, and every small feature visible from outside
  (signs, banners, lanterns, pots, finials). Each tile is labelled with what it frames and its px/block; the JSON lists
  the box and side of each. For any other spot:
  `$MCD zoom house.nbt --at 12,3,0 [--radius 3] [--from n|s|e|w] [--out zoom.png]` (default side: the one with a clear
  line of sight, front first; cells far in front of the spot are left out so they cannot hide it).
- **Change report** — `$MCD diff before.nbt after.nbt --png diff.png [--json] [--fail-empty]`: changed cells by kind
  (added / removed / replaced / state) and block, their groups and boxes, the faces they show on, how many are enclosed
  (never show) or interior-only; with `--png`, changed pixels per standard view and a BEFORE | AFTER pair cropped to
  the change for the two views that changed most. `--fail-empty` exits 1 when nothing changed, when no view shows a
  pixel of the change, or when every changed cell is enclosed — a pass that wrote nothing is a failure, not a no-op.
- **Palette** — `$MCD palette house.nbt`: visible blocks classed into roles by where they sit (walls field, trim and
  edges, roof, base, openings, accents, plants), each with its main materials and measured tone (texture average
  from the client jar). Flags, each with a concrete suggestion: roof in the walls' tone; trim invisible on its wall
  (`trim: stone_bricks on stone_bricks walls -> tuff_bricks or smooth_stone`); an outlier block used a handful of
  times that clashes with everything around it; more than 3 accent colour families; dark detail on a dark ground
  (or light on light).
- **Structure** — `$MCD check house.nbt` now always reports STRUCTURE: floating groups (not connected to the
  lowest layer through face or edge contact), unsupported hanging/mounted blocks (a hanging lantern with nothing
  above, a standing banner or lantern on air, a wall sign with nothing behind), orphans (one block sticking out
  sideways or dangling, touching the build on one face), and enclosed cells (a change there never shows; with two
  files, how many changed cells are enclosed). Report only; the exit code is unchanged.

// instead of typing hundreds of coordinates.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { load, Grid, ns } from "./structure.mjs";
import { t } from "./nbt.mjs";
import { functionalCells } from "./check.mjs";
import { reroof } from "./roofs.mjs";
import { reservedCells, layoutSockets, socketFitout } from "./sockets.mjs";
export { load, Grid };

// ---- directions -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
export const DIRS = { north: [0, 0, -1], south: [0, 0, 1], west: [-1, 0, 0], east: [1, 0, 0] };
export const OPPOSITE = { north: "south", south: "north", east: "west", west: "east", up: "down", down: "up" };
const CW = { north: "east", east: "south", south: "west", west: "north" };
export const face = {
  opposite: (f) => OPPOSITE[f],
  cw: (f) => CW[f],
  ccw: (f) => OPPOSITE[CW[f]],
  /** Mirror a facing across the YZ plane (x -> -x) or XY plane (z -> -z). */
  mirrorX: (f) => (f === "east" ? "west" : f === "west" ? "east" : f),
  mirrorZ: (f) => (f === "north" ? "south" : f === "south" ? "north" : f),
};

// ---- block helpers: return [block, state] pairs for g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs(...)) ----------------------------
// Stairs `facing` = the side of the full-height back; a cornice/bracket lip toward the street uses
// facing = the INWARD direction with half: "top".
export const B = {
  stairs: (mat, facing, half = "bottom", shape = "straight") => [`${mat}_stairs`, { facing, half, shape, waterlogged: "false" }],
  slab: (mat, type = "bottom") => [`${mat}_slab`, { type, waterlogged: "false" }],
  log: (mat, axis = "y") => [`${mat}_log`, { axis }],
  wood: (mat, axis = "y") => [`${mat}_wood`, { axis }],
  pillar: (block, axis = "y") => [block, { axis }],
  trapdoor: (mat, facing, half = "bottom", open = false) => [`${mat}_trapdoor`, { facing, half, open: String(open), powered: "false", waterlogged: "false" }],
  door: (mat, facing, half = "lower", hinge = "left") => [`${mat}_door`, { facing, half, hinge, open: "false", powered: "false" }],
  fence: (mat) => [`${mat}_fence`, {}],
  wall: (mat) => [`${mat}_wall`, {}],
  pane: (block = "glass_pane") => [block, {}],
  lantern: (hanging = false) => ["lantern", { hanging: String(hanging), waterlogged: "false" }],
  chain: (axis = "y", version26 = true) => [version26 ? "iron_chain" : "chain", { axis, waterlogged: "false" }],
  wallTorch: (facing) => ["wall_torch", { facing }],
  block: (name) => [name, {}],
  /**
   * A banner with patterns: [block, state, nbt] for g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner(...)). patterns: [[pattern, colour], ...]
   * (ids such as stripe_center, border, cross, rhombus, flower, globe, gradient, half_horizontal, curly_border).
   * wall: hung on the block behind it, facing `facing`; standing: `rotation` 0..15 (0 faces south). legacy: the

    const block = wall ? `${color}_wall_banner` : `${color}_banner`, state = wall ? { facing } : { rotation: String(rotation) };

    const nbt = legacy

    const block = `${wood}_${wall ? "wall_" : ""}${hanging ? "hanging_" : ""}sign`;

  paint((x, y, z, block, state) => g.set(x, y, z, block, state));

/** Hollow box: walls (and optional floor/ceiling) of a cuboid. */
export function shell(g, a, b, block, { floor = true, ceiling = true, state } = {}) {

  for (let x = x0; x <= x1; x++) for (let y = y0; y <= y1; y++) for (let z = z0; z <= z1; z++) {

  const refused = [];

    get(target, prop) {

      if (prop === "protected") return cells;

1	# Toolkit reference
2	
3	`MCD="node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tools/bin/mcd.mjs"` — pure Node 20+, no install. First use downloads the
4	Minecraft client jar for the needed version from Mojang (sha1-verified) into `~/.cache/minecraft-design/`, or
5	uses `$MC_CLIENT_JAR`, the official launcher's or Prism Launcher's local jars. Nothing copyrighted ships here.
6	
7	## Coordinates and facing (read this once)
8	
9	- Files: every command reads a structure `.nbt` or a Litematica `.litematic` (all regions, in one box); `g.save()`
10	  and `mcd convert` write either, by extension. Block-entity data and entities survive both ways.
11	- Structure-local: `x` east, `y` up, `z` south. `0 ≤ x < size[0]` etc.
12	- Conventional front for new builds: **north (−z)**, the street at `z < 0`. `mcd render` auto-detects the front
13	  from exposed windows/doors; override with `--front n|s|e|w`.
14	- Walking into a building that faces north, you face **south (+z)**; east (+x) is on your **left**.
15	- `facing` on blocks:
16	  - **stairs**: the side of the full-height back. A cornice/bracket whose lip points at the street:
17	    `half: "top"`, `facing` = the direction *into* the wall. A roof slope rising to the north: `facing: "north"`.
18	  - **trapdoor**: the side it hinges from when open; closed `half: "top"` sits in the top of the cell.
19	  - **wall torch / wall sign / wall banner**: the direction it *points out* (away from the wall).
20	  - **repeater / comparator**: `facing` points toward the *input* (signal flows the opposite way).
21	  - **logs**: `axis: x|y|z`.
22	- `mcd states <block>` lists every valid property and value for a block in the target version; `mcd blocks
23	  --grep <re>` lists valid ids (ids change: 26.x renamed `chain` → `iron_chain`); `mcd blocks --check a,b,c` says
24	  which ids are real and suggests near names for the rest. Use them instead of guessing.
25	- `mcd walk build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` floods the cells a player can stand in (jump one up with headroom, drop up
26	  to three, through doors and gates, up ladders, vines, scaffolding and water columns such as a soul-sand water
27	  elevator) from the entrance and says, per room box, whether it's reached, unreachable, or
28	  partly blocked by furniture. rooms.json: `{"entrance": [x,y,z], "rooms": [{"name", "box": [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1]}]}`.
29	- `mcd rooms build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name,...] [--out rooms.png]` shows every room: a dollhouse view
30	  (everything above the room cut away, from a front corner) and, for rooms 5+ wide both ways, an eye view inside.
31	- `layers(g, [x, y, z], legend, rows)` (build library) draws blocks from text the way Litematica stores them: a
32	  legend of characters, one character per block, rows along +x, successive rows along +z, layer by layer. Use it for any
33	  layout of many different blocks (a furnished room, a facade panel); it costs a fraction of a set() per block.
34	  `mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name]` prints each room's floor as that grid ('#' wall, 'D' doorway,
35	  'W' window, 'o' already there, '.' free floor) with the origin to pass to layers().
36	- `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "<room>"` is a room designer's one check after each rebuild: the walk
37	  verdict with the floor cells a player can't reach (marked `x` on the floor grid, which shows the furniture as `o`),
38	  the light levels at the feet, and lantern spots (hanging under the ceiling where there's headroom, else against a
39	  wall) that would lift the dark and dim cells to 8+. Exits 1 until the room is walkable with no dark cell.
40	- `mcd light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name]` (or `--y <feet y>` for a whole floor level) maps block light
41	  the way the game spreads it (each source at its vanilla level, one less per block, stopped by full blocks): each
42	  floor cell's level as 0-9/A-F, with min, mean and the DARK (0, mobs spawn) and dim (1-7) counts. Design lighting
43	  with it: the renderer has no night.
44	
45	## Commands
46	
47	| Command | Does |
48	|---|---|
49	| `render <f.nbt> [--out s.png] [--front d] [--ground y] [--cut y] [--eye x,y,z --look x,y,z [--label t]]... [--view "name:x,y,z->x,y,z"]... [--tiles dir]` | The look sheet: 3 street views at eye height, 4 elevations, 2 front-corner isos, optional cutaway and interior eye views. `--view` adds a named exterior camera with sun shadows (e.g. `"downstream:28,14.5,40->31,18,22"`, the iconic view of a house over a waterfall). `--tiles` also writes each view as its own PNG (zoom into one with Read). |
50	| `compare <before> <after> [--out c.png]` | Before \| after sheets side by side, same cameras. |
51	| `convert <in> <out>` | Structure `.nbt` ↔ Litematica `.litematic`, by extension (schematic version 7 for 1.20.5+, 6 before). Use `.litematic` for builds over 48 blocks a side, which a structure block can't place in one go. |
52	| `roof <in.nbt> <out.nbt> --style <s> [--pitch p] [--eave e] [--material m] [--ridge r] [--dormers 2:e] [--pediment n] [--tower x,z,w,h,top] [--chimney x,z] [--keep box] [--spec roof.json]` / `roof <in.nbt> --detect` | Re-roof a build by style name: detects the eave and footprint, strips the old roof, builds the new one (see roofs.md). `--detect` only reports what it found. |
53	| `check <f.nbt> [after.nbt] [--contract c.json] [--site site.json] [--json]` | (A contract file adds to the automatic redstone protection.) Census, walkability, largest blank surfaces (interior and exterior separately); with two files the FUNCTION report: protected cells unchanged, keep-clear cells clear, warnings for new conductive/triggering/feeding neighbours. `--site` adds the landscape checks (see landscaping.md). Exit 1 on any violation. |
54	| `info <f.nbt>` | Size, DataVersion → version, census, block entities, functional cell count, unknown block ids. |
55	| `blocks [--grep re]` / `states <block>` | Valid ids / states for the version. |
56	| `new <build.mjs> [--from in.nbt] [--size x,y,z] [--out out.nbt]` | Scaffold a generator script wired to the build library (with `--from`, writes are guarded). |
57	| `concept "<subject>" --out c.png [--size s] [--palette p] [--provider codex\|gemini] [--ref img]... [--model m] [--raw]` | A builder's reference sheet (front elevation + 3/4, one scale, no scene). Codex CLI image tool when installed (ChatGPT plan, no key, ~1 min; `--ref` redraws from a given image), else Gemini (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, Nano Banana 2.1 by default). Measured: this prompt shape matters more than the model; 2–3 candidates across providers, picked against the brief, add useful variety. |
58	| `assets [--version v]` | Pre-fetch the client jar. |
59	
60	Version: `--version` › `$MCD_VERSION` › the file's DataVersion › latest release.
61	
62	Render notes: no light engine (light sources show as blocks, not glow); interior eye views skip sun shadows;
63	block-entity blocks (chests, signs, beds, banners, heads) render as simple textured boxes; entities (item
64	frames, armour stands) are not drawn. Keep `--look` inside the build for interior views.

66	## Build library (`tools/src/build.mjs`)
67	
68	```js
69	import { load, Grid, guard, tile, mirrorX, mirrorZ, shell, carve, replace, B, face, DIRS } from ".../tools/src/build.mjs";
70	const g = guard(load("in.nbt"));          // or: new Grid([w, h, d], { dataVersion })
71	g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "south", "top"));   // [block, state] helpers: stairs slab log wood trapdoor door fence wall lantern chain wallTorch pane block
72	g.fill([x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1], "stone_bricks");
73	tile(g, { from: 1, step: 4, to: 19 }, (z, i) => bay(z, i));  // the bay rhythm
74	mirrorX(g, cx, (set) => set(x, y, z, block, state));          // symmetric pair, facings mirrored
75	shell(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", { floor: true, ceiling: false });
76	carve(g, a, b);                            // stores air (clears the cell on placement)
77	replace(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", "stone_bricks");
78	g.save("out.nbt");                          // never overwrite the input
79	console.log(g.refused);                     // guarded writes that were refused (report them)
80	```

104	## Banners, signs and other block entities
105	
106	Banners, signs, chests, beds, bells, mob heads, decorated pots and shulker boxes are entity-rendered in vanilla, and
107	`mcd render` draws them with their entity models and textures:
108	- **Banners:** the cloth in its base colour plus every dyed pattern from the block entity.
109	- **Signs:** their text, glowing text drawn brighter.
110	- **Other entity-rendered blocks:** a neutral box, listed under `unknownBlocks` as "entity-rendered, approximated".
111	
112	Author banners and signs with the build helpers. Each returns `[block, state, nbt]` with valid block-entity NBT
113	that round-trips through save and load:

115	```js
116	g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("cyan", [["stripe_center", "white"], ["border", "black"]], { facing: "north" }));   // wall banner
117	g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("red", [["cross", "yellow"]], { wall: false, rotation: 8 }));                       // standing, faces north
118	g.set(x, y, z, ...B.sign("spruce", ["PERMIT", "OFFICE"], { facing: "north", color: "black", glow: false }));

121	  `stripe_middle`, `border`, `curly_border`, `cross`, `straight_cross`, `rhombus`, `circle`, `flower`, `globe`,

123	  `small_stripes`, `diagonal_left`, `diagonal_right` (the full list is under `textures/entity/banner/`).

127	  string components from 1.21.5 on (`dataVersion` option; the grid's default is 1.21.4).
128	- **Standing `rotation`:** 0 faces south, 4 west, 8 north, 12 east. Wall banners and signs hang on the block behind

131	## Review card
132	
133	One image of a build for a glance or a reviewer (prints one JSON object; non-zero exit and a stderr message on error):
134	
135	- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out card.png [--tiles dir] [--front n] [--reuse]` — render (close-ups, `MCD_TILE_SCALE=2`) and compose the card (street | front-left, front-right | back, plus the roof close-up row; tiles fit 700x700, white). `--reuse` skips the render when `dir/street.png` exists. `{"card","tiles","views":[...]}`
136	- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out eye.png --tiles dir --layout eye` — the eye-level card: only what a player sees from the ground (street | down-the-street left, right | back), sky trimmed, so a roof weighs what it weighs in the game.

138	## Inspection
139	
140	Cheap, deterministic checks to run after every pass, before judging a render by eye. Each has `--json`.
141	
142	- **Glance and close-ups** — `$MCD render house.nbt --closeups --tiles tiles/` adds a row of tiles to the sheet: a
143	  *glance* tile (the street view at 320 px: what reads at a glance) and close-ups at ≥ 12 px per block of the
144	  entrance (door cells), the eave band, each facade's busiest region, and every small feature visible from outside
145	  (signs, banners, lanterns, pots, finials). Each tile is labelled with what it frames and its px/block; the JSON lists
146	  the box and side of each. For any other spot:
147	  `$MCD zoom house.nbt --at 12,3,0 [--radius 3] [--from n|s|e|w] [--out zoom.png]` (default side: the one with a clear
148	  line of sight, front first; cells far in front of the spot are left out so they cannot hide it).
149	- **Change report** — `$MCD diff before.nbt after.nbt --png diff.png [--json] [--fail-empty]`: changed cells by kind
150	  (added / removed / replaced / state) and block, their groups and boxes, the faces they show on, how many are enclosed
151	  (never show) or interior-only; with `--png`, changed pixels per standard view and a BEFORE | AFTER pair cropped to
152	  the change for the two views that changed most. `--fail-empty` exits 1 when nothing changed, when no view shows a
153	  pixel of the change, or when every changed cell is enclosed — a pass that wrote nothing is a failure, not a no-op.
154	- **Palette** — `$MCD palette house.nbt`: visible blocks classed into roles by where they sit (walls field, trim and
155	  edges, roof, base, openings, accents, plants), each with its main materials and measured tone (texture average
156	  from the client jar). Flags, each with a concrete suggestion: roof in the walls' tone; trim invisible on its wall
157	  (`trim: stone_bricks on stone_bricks walls -> tuff_bricks or smooth_stone`); an outlier block used a handful of
158	  times that clashes with everything around it; more than 3 accent colour families; dark detail on a dark ground
159	  (or light on light).
160	- **Structure** — `$MCD check house.nbt` now always reports STRUCTURE: floating groups (not connected to the
161	  lowest layer through face or edge contact), unsupported hanging/mounted blocks (a hanging lantern with nothing
162	  above, a standing banner or lantern on air, a wall sign with nothing behind), orphans (one block sticking out
163	  sideways or dangling, touching the build on one face), and enclosed cells (a change there never shows; with two
164	  files, how many changed cells are enclosed). Report only; the exit code is unchanged.

332	 * break function. protect: Set of "x,y,z" — default: the grid's own functional cells and the cells that must stay
333	 * clear around them (check.mjs functionalCells). `g.refused` lists what was blocked; report it.

335	export function guard(g, protect) {
336	  const cells = protect ?? (() => { const f = functionalCells(g); return new Set([...f.protect.keys(), ...f.keepClear]); })();
337	  const refused = [];
338	  return new Proxy(g, {
339	    get(target, prop) {
340	      if (prop === "refused") return refused;
341	      if (prop === "protected") return cells;
342	      if (prop === "set") return (x, y, z, ...rest) => { if (cells.has(`${x},${y},${z}`)) { refused.push([x, y, z, rest[0]]); return target; } return target.set(x, y, z, ...rest); };

345	      return typeof v === "function" ? v.bind(target) : v;
346	    },
347	  });

400	  // redstone shop sockets (sockets.json, mcd sockets layout): their envelopes are reserved before any part runs, so a

435	      get(target, prop) {
436	        if (prop === "set") return (x, y, z, block, state, nbt) => { write(target, x, y, z, block, state, nbt); return view; };
437	        if (prop === "unset") return (x, y, z) => { write(target, x, y, z, "minecraft:air"); return view; };

453	    const r = { part: name, placed: mine.size, refused: refused.length, refusedAt: refused.slice(0, 8), ...(carved.length ? { carved: carved.length } : {}),

# Toolkit reference

`MCD="node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tools/bin/mcd.mjs"` — pure Node 20+, no install. First use downloads the
Minecraft client jar for the needed version from Mojang (sha1-verified) into `~/.cache/minecraft-design/`, or
uses `$MC_CLIENT_JAR`, the official launcher's or Prism Launcher's local jars. Nothing copyrighted ships here.

## Coordinates and facing (read this once)

- Files: every command reads a structure `.nbt` or a Litematica `.litematic` (all regions, in one box); `g.save()`
  and `mcd convert` write either, by extension. Block-entity data and entities survive both ways.
- Structure-local: `x` east, `y` up, `z` south. `0 ≤ x < size[0]` etc.
- Conventional front for new builds: **north (−z)**, the street at `z < 0`. `mcd render` auto-detects the front
  from exposed windows/doors; override with `--front n|s|e|w`.
- Walking into a building that faces north, you face **south (+z)**; east (+x) is on your **left**.
- `facing` on blocks:
  - **stairs**: the side of the full-height back. A cornice/bracket whose lip points at the street:
    `half: "top"`, `facing` = the direction *into* the wall. A roof slope rising to the north: `facing: "north"`.
  - **trapdoor**: the side it hinges from when open; closed `half: "top"` sits in the top of the cell.
  - **wall torch / wall sign / wall banner**: the direction it *points out* (away from the wall).
  - **repeater / comparator**: `facing` points toward the *input* (signal flows the opposite way).
  - **logs**: `axis: x|y|z`.
- `mcd states <block>` lists every valid property and value for a block in the target version; `mcd blocks
  --grep <re>` lists valid ids (ids change: 26.x renamed `chain` → `iron_chain`); `mcd blocks --check a,b,c` says
  which ids are real and suggests near names for the rest. Use them instead of guessing.
- `mcd walk build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` floods the cells a player can stand in (jump one up with headroom, drop up
  to three, through doors and gates, up ladders, vines, scaffolding and water columns such as a soul-sand water
  elevator) from the entrance and says, per room box, whether it's reached, unreachable, or
  partly blocked by furniture. rooms.json: `{"entrance": [x,y,z], "rooms": [{"name", "box": [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1]}]}`.
- `mcd rooms build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name,...] [--out rooms.png]` shows every room: a dollhouse view
  (everything above the room cut away, from a front corner) and, for rooms 5+ wide both ways, an eye view inside.
- `layers(g, [x, y, z], legend, rows)` (build library) draws blocks from text the way Litematica stores them: a
  legend of characters, one character per block, rows along +x, successive rows along +z, layer by layer. Use it for any
  layout of many different blocks (a furnished room, a facade panel); it costs a fraction of a set() per block.
  `mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name]` prints each room's floor as that grid ('#' wall, 'D' doorway,
  'W' window, 'o' already there, '.' free floor) with the origin to pass to layers().
- `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "<room>"` is a room designer's one check after each rebuild: the walk
  verdict with the floor cells a player can't reach (marked `x` on the floor grid, which shows the furniture as `o`),
  the light levels at the feet, and lantern spots (hanging under the ceiling where there's headroom, else against a
  wall) that would lift the dark and dim cells to 8+. Exits 1 until the room is walkable with no dark cell.
- `mcd light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name]` (or `--y <feet y>` for a whole floor level) maps block light
  the way the game spreads it (each source at its vanilla level, one less per block, stopped by full blocks): each
  floor cell's level as 0-9/A-F, with min, mean and the DARK (0, mobs spawn) and dim (1-7) counts. Design lighting
  with it: the renderer has no night.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `render <f.nbt> [--out s.png] [--front d] [--ground y] [--cut y] [--eye x,y,z --look x,y,z [--label t]]... [--view "name:x,y,z->x,y,z"]... [--tiles dir]` | The look sheet: 3 street views at eye height, 4 elevations, 2 front-corner isos, optional cutaway and interior eye views. `--view` adds a named exterior camera with sun shadows (e.g. `"downstream:28,14.5,40->31,18,22"`, the iconic view of a house over a waterfall). `--tiles` also writes each view as its own PNG (zoom into one with Read). |
| `compare <before> <after> [--out c.png]` | Before \| after sheets side by side, same cameras. |
| `convert <in> <out>` | Structure `.nbt` ↔ Litematica `.litematic`, by extension (schematic version 7 for 1.20.5+, 6 before). Use `.litematic` for builds over 48 blocks a side, which a structure block can't place in one go. |
| `roof <in.nbt> <out.nbt> --style <s> [--pitch p] [--eave e] [--material m] [--ridge r] [--dormers 2:e] [--pediment n] [--tower x,z,w,h,top] [--chimney x,z] [--keep box] [--spec roof.json]` / `roof <in.nbt> --detect` | Re-roof a build by style name: detects the eave and footprint, strips the old roof, builds the new one (see roofs.md). `--detect` only reports what it found. |
| `check <f.nbt> [after.nbt] [--contract c.json] [--site site.json] [--json]` | (A contract file adds to the automatic redstone protection.) Census, walkability, largest blank surfaces (interior and exterior separately); with two files the FUNCTION report: protected cells unchanged, keep-clear cells clear, warnings for new conductive/triggering/feeding neighbours. `--site` adds the landscape checks (see landscaping.md). Exit 1 on any violation. |
| `info <f.nbt>` | Size, DataVersion → version, census, block entities, functional cell count, unknown block ids. |
| `blocks [--grep re]` / `states <block>` | Valid ids / states for the version. |
| `new <build.mjs> [--from in.nbt] [--size x,y,z] [--out out.nbt]` | Scaffold a generator script wired to the build library (with `--from`, writes are guarded). |
| `concept "<subject>" --out c.png [--size s] [--palette p] [--provider codex\|gemini] [--ref img]... [--model m] [--raw]` | A builder's reference sheet (front elevation + 3/4, one scale, no scene). Codex CLI image tool when installed (ChatGPT plan, no key, ~1 min; `--ref` redraws from a given image), else Gemini (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, Nano Banana 2.1 by default). Measured: this prompt shape matters more than the model; 2–3 candidates across providers, picked against the brief, add useful variety. |
| `assets [--version v]` | Pre-fetch the client jar. |

Version: `--version` › `$MCD_VERSION` › the file's DataVersion › latest release.

Render notes: no light engine (light sources show as blocks, not glow); interior eye views skip sun shadows;
block-entity blocks (chests, signs, beds, banners, heads) render as simple textured boxes; entities (item
frames, armour stands) are not drawn. Keep `--look` inside the build for interior views.

## Build library (`tools/src/build.mjs`)

```js
import { load, Grid, guard, tile, mirrorX, mirrorZ, shell, carve, replace, B, face, DIRS } from ".../tools/src/build.mjs";
const g = guard(load("in.nbt"));          // or: new Grid([w, h, d], { dataVersion })
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "south", "top"));   // [block, state] helpers: stairs slab log wood trapdoor door fence wall lantern chain wallTorch pane block
g.fill([x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1], "stone_bricks");
tile(g, { from: 1, step: 4, to: 19 }, (z, i) => bay(z, i));  // the bay rhythm
mirrorX(g, cx, (set) => set(x, y, z, block, state));          // symmetric pair, facings mirrored
shell(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", { floor: true, ceiling: false });
carve(g, a, b);                            // stores air (clears the cell on placement)
replace(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", "stone_bricks");
g.save("out.nbt");                          // never overwrite the input
console.log(g.refused);                     // guarded writes that were refused (report them)
```

Shape brushes (also exported from `build.mjs`): curved forms — `dome`, `cylinder`, `minaret`, `arch` (+ `circleCells`,
`ring`, `disc`, `revolve`) — see `shapes-curved.md`; massing — `setbacks`, `gableRoof`, `hipRoof`, `fins`, `parapet`,
`cornice`, `falseFront`, `stepGable` — see `shapes-massing.md`. Each is `fn(g, opts)`, writes through `g.set` (so
`guard()` still protects function), and returns `{cells, refused, bounds}`.

`guard(grid)` refuses writes into the grid's functional cells and their keep-clear cells (or a set you pass);
it never throws — check `g.refused`. `runParts(g, [["shell", shell.build], ["garden", garden.build]], { palette:
"palette.json" })` runs a build's parts in order so each can only add into air: writes into an earlier part's cells
(air included) are refused and reported, the ground laid before it stays writable, and blocks outside the palette
are reported per part. With `roof: "roof.json"` (a `mcd roof --spec` file) it lays the roof right after the first
part, so later parts build around it instead of the roof tool clearing attics and gables after them; no file yet means
the roof is skipped with a note. A part given `{ carve: true }` as a third element (the stair joiner) may cut through
earlier floors and ceilings (cells with air straight above or below), never walls. `mcd reskin in.nbt out.nbt --swap
spruce=dark_oak,red=blue[,bricks=mud_bricks] [--box ...]` swaps materials on a finished build, form for form, states
kept (a wood or dye word swaps every block named with it; a full block id swaps itself and its stairs, slab and wall);
`mcd variant <run> --name n [--swap ...] [--roof '{json}']` does it into `<run>/variants/n/` with a card, re-running
the build's code when the roof changes. `mcd overworld palette.json [--write]` lists (drops) nether and end blocks. The Grid keeps block-entity NBT (sign text, chest contents) and entities and
writes them back unchanged; cells you don't touch round-trip byte-for-byte.

Grow the box with `g.resize([w, h, d], [dx, dy, dz])` (a shift grows toward −); a shift moves every coordinate,
so re-derive any contract coordinates after shifting.

## Banners, signs and other block entities

Banners, signs, chests, beds, bells, mob heads, decorated pots and shulker boxes are entity-rendered in vanilla, and
`mcd render` draws them with their entity models and textures:
- **Banners:** the cloth in its base colour plus every dyed pattern from the block entity.
- **Signs:** their text, glowing text drawn brighter.
- **Other entity-rendered blocks:** a neutral box, listed under `unknownBlocks` as "entity-rendered, approximated".

Author banners and signs with the build helpers. Each returns `[block, state, nbt]` with valid block-entity NBT
that round-trips through save and load:

```js
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("cyan", [["stripe_center", "white"], ["border", "black"]], { facing: "north" }));   // wall banner
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("red", [["cross", "yellow"]], { wall: false, rotation: 8 }));                       // standing, faces north
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.sign("spruce", ["PERMIT", "OFFICE"], { facing: "north", color: "black", glow: false }));
```
- **Banner patterns:** `stripe_center`, `stripe_top`, `stripe_bottom`, `stripe_left`, `stripe_right`,
  `stripe_middle`, `border`, `curly_border`, `cross`, `straight_cross`, `rhombus`, `circle`, `flower`, `globe`,
  `gradient`, `gradient_up`, `half_horizontal`, `half_vertical`, `triangle_top`, `triangle_bottom`, `bricks`,
  `small_stripes`, `diagonal_left`, `diagonal_right` (the full list is under `textures/entity/banner/`).
- **Colours:** the 16 dye names.
- **NBT format:** banners use the 1.20.5+ `patterns` list (`legacy: true` writes the older `Patterns` /
  `Pattern` / `Color` form). Sign text is written as JSON components below data version 4325 (1.21.5) and as plain
  string components from 1.21.5 on (`dataVersion` option; the grid's default is 1.21.4).
- **Standing `rotation`:** 0 faces south, 4 west, 8 north, 12 east. Wall banners and signs hang on the block behind
  them and face `facing`.

## Review card

One image of a build for a glance or a reviewer (prints one JSON object; non-zero exit and a stderr message on error):

- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out card.png [--tiles dir] [--front n] [--reuse]` — render (close-ups, `MCD_TILE_SCALE=2`) and compose the card (street | front-left, front-right | back, plus the roof close-up row; tiles fit 700x700, white). `--reuse` skips the render when `dir/street.png` exists. `{"card","tiles","views":[...]}`
- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out eye.png --tiles dir --layout eye` — the eye-level card: only what a player sees from the ground (street | down-the-street left, right | back), sky trimmed, so a roof weighs what it weighs in the game.

## Inspection

Cheap, deterministic checks to run after every pass, before judging a render by eye. Each has `--json`.

- **Glance and close-ups** — `$MCD render house.nbt --closeups --tiles tiles/` adds a row of tiles to the sheet: a
  *glance* tile (the street view at 320 px: what reads at a glance) and close-ups at ≥ 12 px per block of the
  entrance (door cells), the eave band, each facade's busiest region, and every small feature visible from outside
  (signs, banners, lanterns, pots, finials). Each tile is labelled with what it frames and its px/block; the JSON lists
  the box and side of each. For any other spot:
  `$MCD zoom house.nbt --at 12,3,0 [--radius 3] [--from n|s|e|w] [--out zoom.png]` (default side: the one with a clear
  line of sight, front first; cells far in front of the spot are left out so they cannot hide it).
- **Change report** — `$MCD diff before.nbt after.nbt --png diff.png [--json] [--fail-empty]`: changed cells by kind
  (added / removed / replaced / state) and block, their groups and boxes, the faces they show on, how many are enclosed
  (never show) or interior-only; with `--png`, changed pixels per standard view and a BEFORE | AFTER pair cropped to
  the change for the two views that changed most. `--fail-empty` exits 1 when nothing changed, when no view shows a
  pixel of the change, or when every changed cell is enclosed — a pass that wrote nothing is a failure, not a no-op.
- **Palette** — `$MCD palette house.nbt`: visible blocks classed into roles by where they sit (walls field, trim and
  edges, roof, base, openings, accents, plants), each with its main materials and measured tone (texture average
  from the client jar). Flags, each with a concrete suggestion: roof in the walls' tone; trim invisible on its wall
  (`trim: stone_bricks on stone_bricks walls -> tuff_bricks or smooth_stone`); an outlier block used a handful of
  times that clashes with everything around it; more than 3 accent colour families; dark detail on a dark ground
  (or light on light).
- **Structure** — `$MCD check house.nbt` now always reports STRUCTURE: floating groups (not connected to the
  lowest layer through face or edge contact), unsupported hanging/mounted blocks (a hanging lantern with nothing
  above, a standing banner or lantern on air, a wall sign with nothing behind), orphans (one block sticking out
  sideways or dangling, touching the build on one face), and enclosed cells (a change there never shows; with two
  files, how many changed cells are enclosed). Report only; the exit code is unchanged.

// Authoring builds as CODE: design one bay, tile it; mirror for symmetry; protect function with a guard.
// Coordinate bookkeeping is where design time and errors go — write a short generator script with these helpers
// instead of typing hundreds of coordinates.
//
//   import { load, Grid, guard, tile, mirrorX, B, face } from "<plugin>/tools/src/build.mjs"
//   const g = guard(load("in.nbt"))                 // refuses writes into functional cells (see check.mjs)
//   runParts(g, [["shell", shellPart], ["porch", porchPart]], { palette: "palette.json" })  // later parts only add
//   tile(g, { from: 1, step: 4, count: 5, axis: "z" }, (z) => bay(g, z))
//   g.save("out.nbt")
import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { load, Grid, ns } from "./structure.mjs";
import { t } from "./nbt.mjs";
import { functionalCells } from "./check.mjs";
import { reroof } from "./roofs.mjs";
import { reservedCells, layoutSockets, socketFitout } from "./sockets.mjs";
export { load, Grid };

// ---- directions -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
export const DIRS = { north: [0, 0, -1], south: [0, 0, 1], west: [-1, 0, 0], east: [1, 0, 0] };
export const OPPOSITE = { north: "south", south: "north", east: "west", west: "east", up: "down", down: "up" };
const CW = { north: "east", east: "south", south: "west", west: "north" };
export const face = {
  opposite: (f) => OPPOSITE[f],
  cw: (f) => CW[f],
  ccw: (f) => OPPOSITE[CW[f]],
  /** Mirror a facing across the YZ plane (x -> -x) or XY plane (z -> -z). */
  mirrorX: (f) => (f === "east" ? "west" : f === "west" ? "east" : f),
  mirrorZ: (f) => (f === "north" ? "south" : f === "south" ? "north" : f),
};

// ---- block helpers: return [block, state] pairs for g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs(...)) ----------------------------
// Stairs `facing` = the side of the full-height back; a cornice/bracket lip toward the street uses
// facing = the INWARD direction with half: "top".
export const B = {
  stairs: (mat, facing, half = "bottom", shape = "straight") => [`${mat}_stairs`, { facing, half, shape, waterlogged: "false" }],
  slab: (mat, type = "bottom") => [`${mat}_slab`, { type, waterlogged: "false" }],
  log: (mat, axis = "y") => [`${mat}_log`, { axis }],
  wood: (mat, axis = "y") => [`${mat}_wood`, { axis }],
  pillar: (block, axis = "y") => [block, { axis }],
  trapdoor: (mat, facing, half = "bottom", open = false) => [`${mat}_trapdoor`, { facing, half, open: String(open), powered: "false", waterlogged: "false" }],
  door: (mat, facing, half = "lower", hinge = "left") => [`${mat}_door`, { facing, half, hinge, open: "false", powered: "false" }],
  fence: (mat) => [`${mat}_fence`, {}],
  wall: (mat) => [`${mat}_wall`, {}],
  pane: (block = "glass_pane") => [block, {}],
  lantern: (hanging = false) => ["lantern", { hanging: String(hanging), waterlogged: "false" }],
  chain: (axis = "y", version26 = true) => [version26 ? "iron_chain" : "chain", { axis, waterlogged: "false" }],
  wallTorch: (facing) => ["wall_torch", { facing }],
  block: (name) => [name, {}],
  /**
   * A banner with patterns: [block, state, nbt] for g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner(...)). patterns: [[pattern, colour], ...]
   * (ids such as stripe_center, border, cross, rhombus, flower, globe, gradient, half_horizontal, curly_border).
   * wall: hung on the block behind it, facing `facing`; standing: `rotation` 0..15 (0 faces south). legacy: the
   * pre-1.20.5 Patterns/Pattern/Color form (for 1.20.4 and older).
   */
  banner: (color, patterns = [], { wall = true, facing = "north", rotation = 0, legacy = false } = {}) => {
    const block = wall ? `${color}_wall_banner` : `${color}_banner`, state = wall ? { facing } : { rotation: String(rotation) };
    const pats = patterns.map((p) => (Array.isArray(p) ? { pattern: p[0], color: p[1] } : p));
    const nbt = legacy
      ? t.compound({ id: t.string("minecraft:banner"), Patterns: t.list("compound", pats.map((p) => ({ Pattern: t.string(LEGACY_PATTERN[p.pattern] ?? p.pattern), Color: t.int(DYE_INDEX.indexOf(p.color)) }))) })
      : t.compound({ id: t.string("minecraft:banner"), patterns: t.list("compound", pats.map((p) => ({ pattern: t.string(`minecraft:${p.pattern.replace(/^minecraft:/, "")}`), color: t.string(p.color) }))) });
    return [block, state, nbt];
  },
  /**
   * A sign with text: [block, state, nbt]. lines: up to 4 strings (front); back: up to 4 more. wood "oak", "spruce" ...
   * wall (facing) or standing (rotation 0..15); hanging: a hanging sign. color: dye name; glow: glowing text.
   * dataVersion: text is written as JSON components before 1.21.5 (4325) and as plain string components after.
   */
  sign: (wood = "oak", lines = [], { wall = true, facing = "north", rotation = 0, hanging = false, color = "black", glow = false, back = [], dataVersion = 4189 } = {}) => {
    const block = `${wood}_${wall ? "wall_" : ""}${hanging ? "hanging_" : ""}sign`;
    const state = wall ? { facing, waterlogged: "false" } : { rotation: String(rotation), waterlogged: "false", ...(hanging ? { attached: "false" } : {}) };
    const msg = (s) => t.string(dataVersion >= 4325 ? String(s ?? "") : JSON.stringify({ text: String(s ?? "") }));
    const side = (ls) => ({ messages: t.list("string", [0, 1, 2, 3].map((i) => msg(ls[i]).value)), color: t.string(color), has_glowing_text: t.byte(glow ? 1 : 0) });
    const nbt = t.compound({ id: t.string(hanging ? "minecraft:hanging_sign" : "minecraft:sign"), is_waxed: t.byte(0), front_text: t.compound(side(lines)), back_text: t.compound(side(back)) });
    return [block, state, nbt];
  },
};
const DYE_INDEX = ["white", "orange", "magenta", "light_blue", "yellow", "lime", "pink", "gray", "light_gray", "cyan", "purple", "blue", "brown", "green", "red", "black"];
const LEGACY_PATTERN = { base: "b", stripe_bottom: "bs", stripe_top: "ts", stripe_left: "ls", stripe_right: "rs", stripe_center: "cs", stripe_middle: "ms",
  stripe_downright: "drs", stripe_downleft: "dls", small_stripes: "ss", cross: "cr", straight_cross: "sc", diagonal_left: "ld", diagonal_right: "rud",
  half_vertical: "vh", half_horizontal: "hh", half_horizontal_bottom: "hhb", triangle_bottom: "bt", triangle_top: "tt", circle: "mc", rhombus: "mr",
  border: "bo", curly_border: "cbo", bricks: "bri", gradient: "gra", gradient_up: "gru", creeper: "cre", skull: "sku", flower: "flo", mojang: "moj", globe: "glb" };

// ---- placement helpers ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/** Call fn(pos, i) for count positions from `from`, `step` apart (the bay rhythm). */
export function tile(_g, { from = 0, step, count, to }, fn) {
  const n = count ?? Math.floor((to - from) / step) + 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) fn(from + i * step, i);
}

/** Run `paint(set)` twice: as written, and mirrored across x = cx (x' = 2cx - x), flipping east/west facings. */
export function mirrorX(g, cx, paint) {
  paint((x, y, z, block, state) => g.set(x, y, z, block, state));
  paint((x, y, z, block, state) => g.set(2 * cx - x, y, z, block, state && state.facing ? { ...state, facing: face.mirrorX(state.facing) } : state));
}
export function mirrorZ(g, cz, paint) {
  paint((x, y, z, block, state) => g.set(x, y, z, block, state));
  paint((x, y, z, block, state) => g.set(x, y, 2 * cz - z, block, state && state.facing ? { ...state, facing: face.mirrorZ(state.facing) } : state));
}

/** Hollow box: walls (and optional floor/ceiling) of a cuboid. */
export function shell(g, a, b, block, { floor = true, ceiling = true, state } = {}) {
  const [x0, y0, z0] = a.map((v, i) => Math.min(v, b[i])), [x1, y1, z1] = a.map((v, i) => Math.max(v, b[i]));
  for (let x = x0; x <= x1; x++) for (let y = y0; y <= y1; y++) for (let z = z0; z <= z1; z++) {
    const edge = x === x0 || x === x1 || z === z0 || z === z1 || (floor && y === y0) || (ceiling && y === y1);
    if (edge) g.set(x, y, z, block, state);
  }
}

/** Set a box to air (carving). Air is stored, so it clears the cell when the structure is placed. */
export const carve = (g, a, b) => g.fill(a, b, "minecraft:air");

/** Replace only where the current block matches `from` (a name or a predicate). */
export function replace(g, a, b, from, block, state) {
  const match = typeof from === "function" ? from : (n) => n === ns(from);
  for (let x = Math.min(a[0], b[0]); x <= Math.max(a[0], b[0]); x++)
    for (let y = Math.min(a[1], b[1]); y <= Math.max(a[1], b[1]); y++)
      for (let z = Math.min(a[2], b[2]); z <= Math.max(a[2], b[2]); z++) if (match(g.blockAt(x, y, z))) g.set(x, y, z, block, state);
}

/**
 * Wrap a grid so writes into protected cells are refused (counted, never thrown), so a decor script cannot
 * break function. protect: Set of "x,y,z" — default: the grid's own functional cells and the cells that must stay
 * clear around them (check.mjs functionalCells). `g.refused` lists what was blocked; report it.
 */
export function guard(g, protect) {
  const cells = protect ?? (() => { const f = functionalCells(g); return new Set([...f.protect.keys(), ...f.keepClear]); })();
  const refused = [];
  return new Proxy(g, {
    get(target, prop) {
      if (prop === "refused") return refused;
      if (prop === "protected") return cells;
      if (prop === "set") return (x, y, z, ...rest) => { if (cells.has(`${x},${y},${z}`)) { refused.push([x, y, z, rest[0]]); return target; } return target.set(x, y, z, ...rest); };
      if (prop === "fill") return (a, b, block, state) => { for (let x = Math.min(a[0], b[0]); x <= Math.max(a[0], b[0]); x++) for (let y = Math.min(a[1], b[1]); y <= Math.max(a[1], b[1]); y++) for (let z = Math.min(a[2], b[2]); z <= Math.max(a[2], b[2]); z++) { if (cells.has(`${x},${y},${z}`)) refused.push([x, y, z, block]); else target.set(x, y, z, block, state); } return target; };
      const v = Reflect.get(target, prop);
      return typeof v === "function" ? v.bind(target) : v;
    },
  });
}

/**
 * Draw blocks from text, the way Litematica stores a schematic (a palette, then one index per cell): one character per
 * block, a legend for the characters. Far fewer tokens than a set() per block, and the layout is visible as written.
 *   layers(g, [x, y, z], { "#": "oak_planks", "b": ["red_bed", { facing: "south", part: "head" }], "c": "chest" }, [
 *     ["#####", "#b c#", "#b  #"],      // y: rows run along +x, successive rows along +z
 *     ["#####", "#   #", "#   #"],      // y + 1 ...
 *   ])
 * A single layer may be passed as one array of rows. Characters not in the legend (space, ".") are left as they are.
 * Writes go through g.set, so runParts' lock and palette report apply. Returns the number of blocks placed.
 */
export function layers(g, [x0, y0, z0], legend, rowsOrLayers) {
  const list = typeof rowsOrLayers[0] === "string" ? [rowsOrLayers] : rowsOrLayers;
  let n = 0;
  list.forEach((rows, dy) => rows.forEach((row, dz) => [...row].forEach((ch, dx) => {
    const e = legend[ch];
    if (e == null) return;
    const [block, state, nbt] = Array.isArray(e) ? e : [e];
    g.set(x0 + dx, y0 + dy, z0 + dz, block, state, nbt);
    n++;
  })));
  return n;
}

/**
 * Run a build's parts in order so each part can only ADD to what earlier parts built: a write into a cell an earlier
 * part placed (air included, so no carving) is refused, counted, never thrown, so a later part can't knock holes in
 * a wall. Cells set before runParts (the ground) stay writable: farmland and paths may replace grass. With a palette
 * (palette.json, or its object: { roles: { role: [blocks] }, objects: [blocks] }), every block placed outside it is
 * reported. Prints one line per part, writes the reports to `report` (default parts-report.json; null for none) and
 * returns them.
 * roof: a roof spec (roof.json, as for `mcd roof --spec`) laid right after the FIRST part (the shell), so every later
 * part builds around the finished roof instead of the roof tool clearing the attic, gables and lofts after them. No
 * file yet (the roof part writes it, maybe in another copy at the same time): skipped with a note, never an error.
 * sockets.json in the working directory (or reserve: a layout or path; null for none) reserves the redstone shops'
 * envelopes: every write into one is refused. A part given { carve: true } (the stair joiner) may cut through earlier parts' floors and ceilings for its
 * stairwells: cells with air straight above or below. Walls stay refused.
 *   runParts(g, [["shell", shell.build], ["stairs", stairs.build, { carve: true }], ["garden", garden.build]],
 *     { palette: "palette.json", roof: "roof.json" })
 */
export function runParts(g, list, { palette, roof, reserve, log = console.log, report = "parts-report.json" } = {}) {
  // `mcd variant` rebuilds a finished build from its code with a roof change ($MCD_ROOF: JSON laid over roof.json)
  // and leaves the build's own reports alone ($MCD_PARTS_REPORT=none)
  if (process.env.MCD_PARTS_REPORT === "none") report = null;
  if (roof && process.env.MCD_ROOF) {
    const base = typeof roof === "string" ? (existsSync(roof) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(roof, "utf8")) : null) : roof;
    if (base) roof = { ...base, ...JSON.parse(process.env.MCD_ROOF) };
  }
  const pal = typeof palette === "string" ? (existsSync(palette) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(palette, "utf8")) : null) : palette;
  const allowed = pal ? new Set([...Object.values(pal.roles ?? {}).flat(), ...(pal.objects ?? [])].map(ns)) : null;
  const owned = new Set(), reports = [], cellsByPart = {};
  // redstone shop sockets (sockets.json, mcd sockets layout): their envelopes are reserved before any part runs, so a
  // write into one is refused like a write into an earlier part, and a carving part can't free them either
  const sock = reserve === undefined ? (existsSync("sockets.json") ? "sockets.json" : null) : reserve;
  const reserved = sock ? reservedCells(typeof sock === "string" ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(sock, "utf8")) : sock) : new Set();
  for (const k of reserved) owned.add(k);
  if (reserved.size) {
    // the fit-out the spec fixes (glass wall lines and back walls, a spawn-proof pit floor, the counters) is laid first
    // and locked like the envelopes: no part can swap a wall line's glass for a conductor
    const L = typeof sock === "string" ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(sock, "utf8")) : sock;
    // the ground laid before runParts (a site filled solid to the street) is dug out of the envelopes
    let dug = 0;
    for (const key of reserved) { const p = key.split(",").map(Number); if (g.inBounds(...p) && !/(^|:)(cave_)?air$/.test(g.blockAt(...p))) { g.set(...p, "air"); dug++; } }
    if (dug) log(`sockets: ${dug} cells of ground dug out of the envelopes`);
    const fit = socketFitout(L, L.fitout ?? {});
    for (const c of fit) { g.set(...c); owned.add(`${c[0]},${c[1]},${c[2]}`); }
    log(`sockets: ${reserved.size} cells reserved for the shops' redstone, ${fit.length} fit-out blocks laid (${typeof sock === "string" ? sock : "layout"})`);
  }
  for (const [name, build, opts0] of list) {
    // the stair joiner carves: a part given { carve: true }, or named for stairs (scaffolds rebuild the list their
    // own way, so the name is what survives)
    const opts = opts0 ?? (/stair/i.test(name) && !/^room:/i.test(name) ? { carve: true } : undefined);
    const mine = new Set(), refused = [], off = new Map(), carved = [];
    const airy = (target, x, y, z) => !target.inBounds(x, y, z) || /(^|:)(cave_)?air$/.test(target.blockAt(x, y, z));
    const write = (target, x, y, z, block, state, nbt) => {
      const k = `${x},${y},${z}`;
      // a carving part (the stair joiner) may cut through an earlier part's floors and ceilings: a cell with air
      // straight above or below it. Walls (solid above and below) stay refused.
      if (owned.has(k) && opts?.carve && !reserved.has(k) && (airy(target, x, y + 1, z) || airy(target, x, y - 1, z))) { owned.delete(k); carved.push([x, y, z]); }
      if (owned.has(k)) { refused.push([x, y, z, ns(block).replace("minecraft:", ""), target.blockAt(x, y, z).replace("minecraft:", "")]); return; }
      const b = ns(block);
      if (allowed && b !== "minecraft:air" && b !== "minecraft:cave_air" && !allowed.has(b)) off.set(b, (off.get(b) ?? 0) + 1);
      target.set(x, y, z, block, state, nbt);
      mine.add(k);
    };
    const view = new Proxy(g, {
      get(target, prop) {
        if (prop === "set") return (x, y, z, block, state, nbt) => { write(target, x, y, z, block, state, nbt); return view; };
        if (prop === "unset") return (x, y, z) => { write(target, x, y, z, "minecraft:air"); return view; };
        if (prop === "fill") return (a, b, block, state) => {
          for (let x = Math.min(a[0], b[0]); x <= Math.max(a[0], b[0]); x++)
            for (let y = Math.min(a[1], b[1]); y <= Math.max(a[1], b[1]); y++)
              for (let z = Math.min(a[2], b[2]); z <= Math.max(a[2], b[2]); z++) write(target, x, y, z, block, state);
          return view;
        };
        const v = Reflect.get(target, prop);
        return typeof v === "function" ? v.bind(target) : v;
      },
    });
    // in a variant (a roof change) a part written for the old roof may throw: keep what it placed, say so, go on
    if (process.env.MCD_ROOF) { try { build(view); } catch (e) { log(`part ${name}: FAILED with this roof (${String(e.message).split("\n")[0]}); kept what it placed`); } }
    else build(view);
    for (const k of mine) owned.add(k);
    if (process.env.MCD_PARTS_CELLS) cellsByPart[name] = [...mine].map((k) => { const c = g.get(...k.split(",").map(Number)); return [k, c ? c.block.replace("minecraft:", "") + (c.state ? JSON.stringify(c.state) : "") : "air"]; });
    const r = { part: name, placed: mine.size, refused: refused.length, refusedAt: refused.slice(0, 8), ...(carved.length ? { carved: carved.length } : {}),
      offPalette: [...off].map(([b, n]) => `${b.replace("minecraft:", "")} x${n}`) };
    reports.push(r);
    log(`part ${name}: ${r.placed} placed` + (carved.length ? ` (${carved.length} cut through earlier floors)` : "") +
      (r.refused ? `; REFUSED ${r.refused} writes into earlier parts (x,y,z wanted had: ${r.refusedAt.map((p) => `${p[0]},${p[1]},${p[2]} ${p[3]} ${p[4]}`).join("; ")})` : "") +
      (r.offPalette.length ? `; OFF-PALETTE: ${r.offPalette.join(", ")}` : ""));
    if (roof && reports.length === 1) r.offPalette.push(...layRoof(g, roof, owned, log, allowed));   // the shell's to fix
  }
  if (report) writeFileSync(report, JSON.stringify(reports, null, 1));
  // $MCD_PARTS_CELLS=<file>: every part's cells, for measuring how much code each block cost (lab token audits)
  if (process.env.MCD_PARTS_CELLS) writeFileSync(process.env.MCD_PARTS_CELLS, JSON.stringify(cellsByPart));
  return reports;
}

// The roof from its spec on top of the shell, inside runParts: the cells it lays are locked like a part's; the shell
// cells it clears (above the eave) are freed for the parts that come after.
function layRoof(g, roof, owned, log, allowed) {
  const spec = typeof roof === "string" ? (existsSync(roof) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(roof, "utf8")) : null) : roof;
  if (!spec) { log(`roof: skipped, no ${roof} yet (the roof part writes it); every later part builds without it`); return []; }
  const before = new Map([...g].map((c) => [c.pos.join(","), c.block + JSON.stringify(c.state ?? {})]));
  const r = reroof(g, { ...spec, keep: spec.keep ?? [] });
  if (r.shift?.some(Boolean)) throw new Error(`roof: the overhang grew the site and moved every block by ${r.shift}; make the site larger so the roof fits`);
  let laid = 0, freed = 0;
  const off = new Map();
  for (const c of g) {
    const k = c.pos.join(",");
    if (before.get(k) !== c.block + JSON.stringify(c.state ?? {})) {
      owned.add(k); laid++;
      if (allowed && !allowed.has(ns(c.block))) off.set(ns(c.block), (off.get(ns(c.block)) ?? 0) + 1);
    }
    before.delete(k);
  }
  for (const k of before.keys()) if (owned.delete(k)) freed++;                 // cleared by the roof: open for later parts
  log(`roof: ${laid} placed (${spec.preset ?? spec.style ?? "roof"}), ${freed} shell cells above the eave cleared${r.refused ? `, ${r.refused} kept` : ""}` +
    (off.size ? `; OFF-PALETTE: ${[...off].map(([b, n]) => `${b.replace("minecraft:", "")} x${n}`).join(", ")} (fix roof.json)` : ""));
  return [...off].map(([b, n]) => `${b.replace("minecraft:", "")} x${n} (roof.json)`);
}
